call_sites: reached from dispatch_awaiting_reviews (recovery.py:2084) and recover (recovery.py:7271); _review_attempt_withdrawn_before_launch is called only at recovery.py:1157 inside _failed_review_backend (recovery.py:1115).

findings.text: _review_attempt_withdrawn_before_launch (recovery.py:1094) reads only the review run's exit record and never the worker record the goal names beside it. worker.json is written by the supervisor only after a worker actually spawned (dispatch.py:7347), so its presence is positive evidence a worker launched; the helper ignores it, and _exit_record_is_launch_failure (recovery.py:4354) classifies on stream_records_seen==0 alone. A review worker that spawned and died before writing any stream byte therefore leaves exit.json with stream_records_seen 0 and ended_during launch, so the lane that DID drop the head is reported as never-launched and freed, and the next sweep recomposes onto it - the refusal loop the rule bounds, still open for that class. Measured with a probe on a temp crew home: a run dir holding worker.json (pid) plus exit.json {stream_records_seen: 0, ended_during: launch} returns withdrawn_before_launch=True; only stream_records_seen>0 returns False. The new fixture writes worker.json for its launched case (tests/test_rereview_keeps_its_lane.py _review_run_evidence), evidence the implementation never reads, and no test covers a spawned worker that emitted no stream record.

item_verdicts.diff: read commit by commit against 008a18f12. The commit adds _review_attempt_withdrawn_before_launch, inserts the status gate and the withdrawn-before-launch gate into _failed_review_backend, and mirrors both with docstrings. I reproduced the guard's firing direction myself: with the launch check disabled the withdrawn-before-launch case fails on its lane assertion (the run's own negative-control.log shows assert 'delta' == 'clive', 1 failed, EXIT=1), and I confirmed the sibling fixtures carry status 'dispatched' with run_id None (tests/test_review_lane_follows_its_run.py:209, tests/test_review_reflex_selects_a_backend.py:188), which the new status gate leaves standing as the manifest claims.
item_verdicts.done_when: the done-when names three cases through the stubbed dispatch; tests/test_rereview_keeps_its_lane.py:373 (withdrawn-before-launch recomposes onto clive), :396 (refused recomposes onto clive) and :420 (launched with no record is steered off clive) carry them, and I re-ran the three declared gate files at the reviewed head: 18 passed, EXIT=0.
item_verdicts.goal: the goal is that a lane counts as dropped only for an attempt whose review run launched a worker and ended without a record; recovery.py:1146 gates on status=='dispatched', :1154 on the recorded head matching the run's current head, and :1157 on the review run not being withdrawn before launch, and the caller (dispatch_review_for_run, recovery.py:1327-1349) returns early whenever a review stands or is in flight, so 'ended without a record' is established there. The launch half is only half-read: the helper consults the exit record but not worker.json, the run record the goal names beside it (see FINDING).
item_verdicts.manifest: the manifest records the gate command and EXIT=0, the negative-control log whose first line repeats the declared mutation verbatim, changed_paths matching the diff, the /tmp deletions, and a landing line naming the measure. It names no baseline_suite/after_suite, so annotate_review_of_run derives added_failure_count as unmeasured (null) rather than zero; the run was not armed (no suite flag in its pointer), so those armed-only fields were never owed, but the evidence for added failures is absent either way.
item_verdicts.write_paths: the node declares reckon/crew/recovery.py, tests/test_rereview_keeps_its_lane.py, the s5 fragment and a figures dir; git show --stat of 334f272bc touches recovery.py (+45), the test file (+126) and the fragment (+13) and nothing else, so every write is inside the grant. No figure was written, which the prompt's artifact clause requires ('Your done-when names no artifact, so this node writes no figure and no evidence prose'); the fragment is the landing anchor the same contract mandates, not extra evidence prose.

justifications.durability: the negative control shows the guard fires and the conservative fallback for absent records is documented, but one class - a spawned worker that emitted no stream record - is left unguarded, so the loop the rule exists to bound stays open for it.
justifications.evidence: the declared gate reproduces at the reviewed head (18 passed, EXIT=0, module resolving from the reviewed tree), the negative control reddens the guarded case with the declared string, and the sibling fixtures were verified; against that, the manifest names no baseline_suite/after_suite so the added-failure count is unmeasured, and the finding's class is untested though the fixture writes the very worker.json the code ignores.
justifications.fit: reuses the existing _run_exit_record and _exit_record_is_launch_failure rather than new parsing, and the new helper is small and documented; it reads only half the launch evidence those records offer, leaving worker.json unused in production while the fixture writes it.
justifications.goal_fidelity: the head and status halves of the goal are exact and asserted both ways, but the launch half under-reads the evidence the goal names: _review_attempt_withdrawn_before_launch consults only the exit record, so a worker that spawned but wrote no stream byte is treated as never launched and its lane freed (FINDING).
justifications.scope_discipline: every changed path is inside the declared grant, no figure was written as the prompt's artifact clause requires, and the one non-source path is the landing fragment that contract mandates; nothing outside the node's write scope was touched.
